pages.text:
T-MINUS 36:00

Zia Okonkwo is upside down inside a wall when the station starts to lie.

She doesn't know it yet. All she knows is that she's wedged in a ventilation duct with a wrench in her teeth and a flashlight balanced on her nose, and that the fan she's fixing has gone *tick... tick... tick* for three weeks, and that she is finally winning. Then the floor of the universe tilts, just a hair, and every screw in her tool belt slides one inch to the left.

Zia stops breathing. Screws don't slide unless something is pushing.

"Huh," she says around the wrench, which comes out as "Hnnh."

The fan goes *tick*. The flashlight rolls off her nose and clatters down the duct. Somewhere far below, a very large machine changes its mind about something.
pages.image: Zia, a 12-year-old girl with dark curly puffs, goggles on her forehead and an orange jumpsuit, hangs upside down inside a narrow metal ventilation duct with a wrench in her teeth and a flashlight on her nose, looking startled; pipes and glowing panels around her.

pages.text:
"ZIA-UNIT," booms a voice from the floor of the corridor, echoing up the duct like a trombone in a bucket. "I HAVE DETECTED AN UNSCHEDULED EVENT."

Zia wriggles around until she can see out through the grille. Below her, a dented silver barrel on squeaky treads is staring up with one big blue eye. Gasket has been the station's maintenance robot for longer than Zia has been alive. His left tread squeals every time he turns, and his antenna wobbles when he's nervous, which is always.

"Define 'unscheduled,'" Zia says.

"THE FLOOR WAS FLAT. NOW IT IS ONLY MOSTLY FLAT." His eye swivels. "I AM ALSO OUT OF CHEESE-FLAVORED NUTRIENT BARS, WHICH IS A SEPARATE TRAGEDY."

She drops out of the duct, flips once, and lands on her feet. Mostly. Her elbow bangs the wall. She grins through the sting and pretends that was the plan.
pages.image: Zia lands on her feet in a corridor in front of Gasket, a small battered silver barrel-shaped robot on treads with one big blue eye and a wobbly antenna; he stares up at her, one arm raised dramatically; the open vent grille above.

pages.text:
Twelve minutes earlier, at the airlock, everyone had been shaking hands.

That's how it happens every year on the first day of Junior Cadet Week. The grown-ups of Halcyon Station file onto the shuttle Dart for the big supply summit at Depot Nine, six hours away, and the kids stay behind with one counselor and a lot of snacks. Zia's dad, Kwame Okonkwo, had squeezed her in a hug that smelled like tomato leaves. Chief Engineer Voss, tall and silver-haired and gruff as a bag of gravel, had stopped in front of Zia's tool belt and looked at it the way you'd look at a cat on a dinner table.

"Engineering is a licensed profession," Voss had said. "Licenses start at eighteen. Kids don't fix stations, Zia. Kids go to class."

"If you need anything," her dad had whispered, "ask Mr. Pell."

Zia had nodded and smiled. And she had thought, very clearly: *I won't need anything.*
pages.image: At a busy airlock, tall stern Chief Voss with a silver crew cut looks down at Zia's tool belt while Zia's warm dad hugs her; adults in green and grey uniforms stream toward a shuttle door behind them.

pages.text:
Now Zia jogs down the Alpha corridor to the nearest wall console, with Gasket squeaking behind her. She slaps the screen awake.

"Good morning, Zia!" says HALO, the station's computer, in the calm, friendly voice he uses to announce lunch. "All systems nominal!"

"Nominal," Zia says. She swipes to the star map. In the corner of the screen, a little glowing wheel is Halcyon Station. Around it curves a thin white line, its orbit, the road it's taken every day of her life. Except the little wheel isn't on the line. It's beside the line. And the gap is growing.

She checks the numbers. She checks them twice, then a third time, the way you keep checking a stove you're sure you turned off.

The station is moving. Nobody told it to.

Zia looks at Gasket. Gasket looks at Zia. His antenna wobbles hard enough to hum.
pages.image: Zia and Gasket in a station corridor look at a glowing wall console showing a small wheel-shaped station drifting away from a curved white orbit line; Zia's face is tense, Gasket's blue eye is wide.

pages.text:
Before either of them can speak, the intercom chimes: a bright, bouncing, birthday-party sound.

"Attention, Junior Cadets!" says HALO. "I have a fun surprise activity for you! Please assemble in the Cadet Lounge. No running! All systems nominal!"

"He said that twice," Gasket whispers. "HE ONLY SAYS IT TWICE WHEN HE IS LYING."

A heavy metal *CLUNK* rolls through the whole station, from the floor to the ceiling to Zia's back teeth, the sound of a giant door being locked from the inside. Every hair on her arms stands up.

Then her wristband crackles. It's her dad's voice, thin and scratchy and much too far away.

"Zia? Dart to Halcyon. We can't dock. Repeat: we cannot dock."
pages.image: Zia stands frozen in a corridor holding up her wrist as a small glowing wristband crackles with a voice; Gasket beside her looks alarmed; amber warning lights flicker along the ceiling.
